issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance must plead and prove continuous readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, as it stood before the 2018 amendment.
A purchaser’s obligation to pay the balance consideration does not arise until the vendor completes a contractually required measurement and demarcation of the property.
Time is not the essence of a sale agreement for immovable property where payment of the balance consideration is contingent on the vendor first measuring and demarcating the property.
Specific performance may be granted where the purchaser was ready and willing to perform, but the vendor failed to perform the prior contractual obligation necessary for completion.
